subject: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Grace Salter <grace@horizon-analytics.com>, Tom Brewster <tom.brewster@stellarmedia.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout

Hi Grace / Tom,

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood at the Horizon Summit last week — we really appreciated the high-quality conversations from your attendees. We ran our post-event ledger against HubSpot and have an initial pipeline attribution table attached (Horizon_Summit_Attendee_ledger.csv).

Quick summary:
- Redwood-match: 142 unique attendee records matched to HubSpot contacts / owners
- Deals touched (30d post-event): 8 deals (aggregate ACV $142k) where the first meaningful contact occurred within 21 days of the event date
- Discrepancy: Horizon’s internal ledger shows 13 influenced leads and a higher pipeline number than what our CRM query returns

Could you confirm whether your attendee ledger is a raw scan of badge swipes (with email) or if any manual merges/exports were applied? We want to reconcile on the matching keys (email vs phone vs hashed badge id) so finance can finalize the event-level ledger for revenue recognition.

Attached: Horizon_Summit_Attendee_ledger.csv (CSV, 42KB) — contains the attendee email, badge_id, company, and the timestamp we received the opt-in.

Suggested next steps:
1) If you can share the list of Horizon lead IDs that you consider event-generated, we’ll run a UID-level tieout and produce a variance table.
2) If there are specific leads you believe were double-counted on our side, flag the lead IDs and we’ll investigate.
3) If needed, we can hop on a 30-min tieout call mid-week.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Field Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Grace Salter <grace@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brewster <tom.brewster@stellarmedia.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the summary and for sharing the ledger. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Our ledger is exported from the badge-scan system and then cross-checked against our registration list; it’s primarily email-based matches. We did one manual pass to merge duplicates (same attendee using two emails) — I can include a column showing the merge parent_id.
- We believe 13 leads should be considered "event-influenced" because the champions first replied to our follow-up within 5 days and later converted to MQL. We can share our internal lead IDs.

I attached a short note with the five leads we’re most concerned about (we think they may have been filtered out by your timing window). We’re happy to do a tieout call. Tom — looping you in since you handled the badge export.

Attachment: horizon-5-key-leads.txt (plain text, 1.2KB)

Best,
Grace

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace Salter <grace@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout

Hi Grace — thanks for the extra context. I pulled the matching logic we ran and pasted the core points below (also attached as redwood-match-logic.txt):

Summary of Redwood matching / attribution logic used for the initial ledger:
1) Primary key: contact email (exact match, case-insensitive)
2) Secondary matching: phone number (last 10 digits) and, if provided, hashed badge_id
3) Attribution window: first meaningful engagement (demo request, discovery call, demo completed) within 21 days of event => event influence flag
4) De-dupe: contacts with merged emails in HubSpot are unified under the canonical contact id before attribution counting

Based on that, the five leads you flagged fall into two buckets:
- 3 leads had the first demo request 28–32 days post-event (outside our 21-day window)
- 2 leads were matched only via a phone number that did not exist in your ledger export (email mismatch)

If Horizon is comfortable expanding the attribution window to 30 days for this event, those three deals would flip to "influenced" and your pipeline number aligns with ours. We can run that revised window and provide a variance table.

Quick ask for tieout: can you export the Horizon lead IDs (your CRM) and include the canonical email and phone so we can join deterministically? That will let us produce a 1:1 reconciliation table.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0188
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace Salter <grace@horizon-analytics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout

Thanks — jumping in from Finance & Ops perspective. For revenue recognition and our event ROI model we need a few concrete outputs so we can close the month:

1) Horizon lead IDs (CSV) with canonical email and phone
2) If you did a manual merge pass, include the merge parent_id so we can align with HubSpot canonical ids
3) If you want the attribution window extended (21 -> 30 days) note that in writing so finance has the agreed rule for this event

I attached a draft variance workbook (variance-draft-2026-07-07.xlsx) that outlines how we’ll present the before/after counts and the impact to recognized pipeline. If we expand the window to 30 days, the draft shows the delta estimate (approx +$38k ACV).

Can Horizon confirm by end of day tomorrow whether you want the 30-day window applied? If yes, we’ll generate the final tieout and send a signed reconciliation memo that both teams can keep on file.

Thanks — Karthik

Attachment: variance-draft-2026-07-07.xlsx (Excel, 96KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Grace Salter <grace@horizon-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon Summit — attendee-ledger vs CRM pipeline tieout

Appreciate the fast turnaround, everyone. Grace — thanks for offering to export the Horizon lead IDs. To keep timelines tight, here’s the agreed plan:

Action items (owners / deadlines):
- Horizon (Grace / Tom) — export lead IDs + canonical email/phone + merge_parent_id if applicable; share CSV by EOD Fri 2026-07-09
- Redwood (Ben) — run the 21-day and 30-day attribution queries and produce a 1:1 reconciliation table and variance workbook by Mon 2026-07-12
- Redwood Finance (Karthik) — prepare the reconciliation memo and delta ACV impact; include language for whether 30-day window will be used for internal recognition
- Both teams — 30-min tieout call scheduled Tue 2026-07-13 11:00 PDT (https://meet.redwood.com/zoom/7a8b9c-call-link)

If Horizon confirms the 30-day rule in writing by EOD Fri we’ll use that as the final standing for this event. Otherwise we’ll present both counts in the memo and finance will proceed with the conservative (21-day) figure for recognition.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Field Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
